title: Heritage approval for 45-storey Duke Street tower
subtitle: Vision Zero crosswalks, asset management, reserve fund transfers, sign and property standards by-laws, Whitney Place zoning, sanitary master plan.
overview: Council approved a heritage permit for 10 Duke Street West, allowing partial demolition of the existing building and a 45-storey mixed-use tower. The front and east façades and part of the west façade will be kept and built into the base, subject to conditions. Council also directed that notices of intention to designate be published for two other heritage properties.

Council adopted new asset management plans for non-core assets and moved funds between city reserves. It approved four new pedestrian crossovers under the Vision Zero program and asked staff to look at shifting traffic calming money to the Vision Zero hot spot program. It also updated the Property Standards and Sign by-laws, approved zoning changes for 115-131 Whitney Place, and approved the Integrated Sanitary Master Plan for its public review period.

A delegate asked Council to review how the Humane Society investigates dog bites. The Mayor said the Director of By-law Enforcement, who manages that contract, would take the concerns under advisement. A hospital foundation also promoted its June 7 fundraising day.

decisions.detail: Council approved partial demolition and a 45-storey mixed-use building that keeps the front, east and part of the west façades, subject to conservation, protection and permit-clearance conditions {{vote:m2}}.

Council received the progress update, approved 2024 safety improvements and four pedestrian crossovers with no-stopping zones, and asked staff to study moving traffic calming funds to the hot spot program {{vote:m10}}.

Council amended the reserve funds policy and transferred $400,863 to the Investment Stabilization Reserve Fund and $4,488,866 to the Tax Capital Reserve Fund, both from the Tax Stabilization Reserve Fund.
Council approved asset management plans for non-core assets and the Corporate Asset Management policy.
Council approved zoning amendments for 115-131 Whitney Place under both zoning by-laws, with the newer by-law taking effect only once the Growing Together secondary plans by-law is in force.
Council adopted the changes to the Sign By-law and added them to the Municipal Code.
Council adopted amendments that repeal and replace specific sections of the Property Standards By-law.
Council approved the environmental study report and directed staff to file it for the 30-day public review period.

debate: On the Duke Street permit, one councillor who sits on the heritage committee opposed it, calling the plan facadism that heritage members generally want to avoid. The councillor noted the building is listed, has a notice of intention to designate, and meets six of nine criteria.

Staff said facadism is not the preferred form of conservation. They supported the plan because designation would protect the retained features permanently and site plan conditions could protect them during construction. Retained interior elements include brass fittings and travertine tile.

Other councillors supported the permit, saying enough heritage character is kept, the tower adds downtown homes and interest, and the retained façades would conserve the building's significance. One suggested the heritage committee explore digital and virtual reality recreation of lost landmarks.

A delegate said the Humane Society's dog bite investigations are inconsistent. The delegate said a mandatory complaint form was not used in their own case, and that victims have no appeal process. The delegate asked Council to review the contract.
